topology: R1 and R2 clients, R3 non-client edge, and redundant RR1/RR2 share AS65000. Seven OSPF point-to-point links carry only loopback/transit reachability. R4 AS65100 originates the service LAN. Both clients peer only with both reflectors; the reflectors and R3 form the non-client mesh. Practice begins with sixteen Established peer views but no client roles or shared cluster ID.
implemented: Thirty-third ENARSI entry with independent practice/reference attempts, nine-row addressing plan, twenty typed goals, ordinary IOS/Windows commands and current-domain/path/query permalinks. Existing UI, icons, terminal styles and offline single HTML are preserved.

Both reflectors use cluster10.255.0.100, R1/R2 client roles, and R3/inter-reflector non-client roles. Actual received advertisements preserve NEXT_HOP, AS_PATH, LOCAL_PREF and MED; iBGP routes install at AD200 and external routes at AD20. The edge, rather than the reflectors, supplies next-hop-self for the external prefix.

Client routes reach clients/non-clients; non-client service reaches only clients. Raw shared-cluster client copies arrive but are excluded before best-path preference. Temporarily removing only R1 roles produces a partial service failure with all sixteen peer views up; temporarily making R3 a client permits service reflection to peer RRs, which reject shared-cluster copies.

Removing both R3 next-hop-self statements leaves the external next hop inaccessible on both RRs. Those candidates cannot enter the RIB or be reflected. Both client service paths disappear while client-to-client and local-control traffic keep working.

A temporary RR2 cluster10.255.0.200 plus neighbor weight200 accepts RR1 client paths and reflects them with CLUSTER_LIST[B,A] and preserved ORIGINATOR_ID. Both clients receive but reject their own reflected prefixes. Returning only RR2 cluster ID to A rejects the previously preferred copies before weight200 can apply; direct weight0 client candidates remain usable.

Full RR1 physical isolation followed by185 simulated seconds leaves eight Established directed peer views and actual forwarding/HTTP through RR2. Restoring all four ports rebuilds OSPF recursion and BGP paths. A separate test proves selecting RR2 as advertising peer does not force physical forwarding through RR2 when the preserved next hop resolves through RR1.

Seven live and thirteen observed goals: practice0, diagnosis1, repaired baseline14, full20 and reference7 with no pre-earned observations. Each traffic state requires three unique original requests in all eight directions, actual destination acceptance, recursive CEF physical forwarding and correlated replies; expected failures require actual No route drops. Both HTTP client responses must be fully reassembled. Six exercises require proved alternative/failure states and fresh restored traffic. Epochs reject stale packets, YAML preserves earned observations and runtime state is rebuilt.

Existing BGP engine and CLI behavior are reused; no unsupported commands or protocol placeholders were introduced. Rendered IOS replay, saved reload, real hard clears, help/Tab, no-forms and invalid-input atomicity are covered.
scope: IOS IPv4 unicast route reflection, redundant shared-cluster RRs, a temporary two-cluster hierarchy, loop prevention, edge next-hop reachability and actual forwarding/recovery. Cisco primary documentation and RFC4456 reviewed. No fresh CML capture or complete IOS/NX-OS equivalence is claimed.

correctedReplayCase.note: Replay into running routers is followed by confirmed clear ip ospf process so the configured router IDs take effect. The original test omitted this operational reset. All full-suite failures, if present, are confined to that superseded replay setup.
